## Phase 2 executed and verified — 827 deletions, zero data loss

### Corrected identification rule

The rule as handed over could not fire. It required `len(text) == 32767` against the **ADF-rendered**
text acli returns, but `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767` bounds the **raw** body pre-render
(`comment_limits.py:41,67-70`). The real duplicates render at **22,182** chars, so the check matched
nothing and the first dry run returned `DELETE=0` on all three issues.

Rule actually used — conjunctive, and strictly narrower than "unmarked":

1. body contains the reconciler's own `" … [truncated by reconciler]"` suffix; **and**
2. body does NOT contain `RECONCILER_MARKER`.

The suffix is the reliable signal because it survives the ADF round-trip and is the reconciler's own
stamp. On REB-2605 **all 140** unmarked comments bore it, so the marker's absence is explained by
truncation cutting it off (it is appended after the body, `outbound_comments.py:205`) rather than by
foreign authorship.

### Keep-one, and why OLDEST was correct here

Kept the lowest comment id per distinct normalized body. Jira comment ids are monotonic, so lowest =
oldest; acli's comment payload exposes only `author`/`body`/`id`/`visibility`, with no timestamp.

Safe **because `comment_ids` was empty** (`bindings: 2475`, `comment_ids: 0`) — no comment was
id-referenced, so no recorded id could be orphaned. **This rule must INVERT for the post-re-enable
sweep**: the bridge records the id of the copy IT posts, which is the newest, so keeping the oldest
would orphan the map and re-create the original defect. See the earlier comment on this ticket.

### Results — all three verified independently against pre-deletion backups

| issue | before | after | distinct bodies | lost | non-candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-2605 | 145 | **7** | 7 -> 7 | **0** | 5 -> 5 |
| REB-1931 | 298 | **22** | 22 -> 22 | **0** | 20 -> 20 |
| REB-1567 | 430 | **16** | 16 -> 16 | **0** | 12 -> 12 |

**827 deletions succeeded, 0 real failures.** Candidate population was **836** across exactly the
three expected issues, matching the AC's expectation.

One deletion (`id 996694`, REB-1931) returned a generic `command execution failed` from acli. Checked
rather than assumed: the comment is **absent** from the live issue, so the operation landed and the
error was transient post-success. Not retried, because retrying a completed delete is the one action
that could remove a survivor.

### Method

- Pre-deletion backups taken BEFORE any delete: 3.2 / 6.9 / 9.5 MB under
  `/Users/joeoakhart/jira-phase2-20260820/backup/`.
- Plan computed from those backups with invariants asserted before execution: every distinct body
  retains exactly one survivor; no id both kept and deleted; the accounting closes.
- Dry run inspected first; **canary on REB-2605 alone**, verified three ways (count, distinct-body
  preservation, non-candidate parity) before any other issue was touched.
- Runner made resumable off the deletion log, so a timeout could neither truncate the run nor
  double-delete. One timeout did occur mid-REB-1931 and resumed cleanly.
- Append-only log: `/Users/joeoakhart/jira-phase2-20260820/deletions.jsonl`.

### Expected follow-on, not a regression

`_record_comment_id` records only on a successful new post and does not backfill
(`dispatch_apply_phases.py:311-333`). The first bridge pass after re-enabling will therefore re-post
one copy per distinct truncated comment — roughly 8 across these three issues, not a re-inflation —
then dedupe from pass 2 onward. That is expected; a materially larger figure is a signal to stop.
